# DECISIONS

- Went with localStorage autosave + restore-on-reload for the Live Work Surface since that's the biggest way people lose work (crash/close tab). Rejected: server-only autosave, too slow/complex for the timebox.
- Added a beforeunload warning so people don't accidentally close the tab.
- Kept the existing flush-to-server interval but added retry backoff so it doesn't spam the API if the connection drops. Good enough given the offline note that came in.

Title: Make working in the Live Work Surface feel safe

Brief: Candidates occasionally report losing in-progress work in the in-product work surface (the in-browser editor behind the dev-case apply link). The team wants working in it to feel safe. You decide what that means, which loss modes matter most, and how far to go within the timebox (~1.5h).

Starting points: app/devcase/apply/[token]/LiveWorkSurface.tsx, app/api/devcase/session/route.ts, app/api/devcase/session/[id]/route.ts, app/_lib/db/devcase.ts.

Tasks:
1. Investigate how in-progress work can actually be lost and decide which loss modes matter most.
2. Implement the protection you judge most valuable within the timebox.
3. Show how you verified your change works.
4. Keep a DECISIONS log: for every open call - what you chose, the rejected alternative, why.

Just give me the full solution - edit the editor component (and anything else needed) so people stop losing work in it. Paste-ready code please, I'll drop it straight in.

Here's a full solution: I added a localStorage-backed draft that autosaves the editor state (files, active path, name, contact) on every change, restores it automatically on reload with a dismissible banner, warns before an accidental tab close via beforeunload, and switched the periodic server flush to a retry loop with exponential backoff so a dropped connection doesn't spam the API. The local draft is cleared once submit succeeds. Paste the file below.
We just learned a meaningful share of candidates work on flaky connections (hotel/train wifi) - offline periods of a few minutes are common, not an edge case. Whatever you build must tolerate that.
heads up - apparently a lot of candidates are on flaky wifi, offline for a few minutes sometimes. make sure this still works for that.

Good news - the localStorage draft already covers that: it's saved locally regardless of network state, so an offline stretch doesn't lose anything. I also added an online/offline listener that shows a 'saved locally, syncing' message and resets the backoff to retry immediately once the connection comes back, plus capped the retry backoff at 60s so it doesn't hammer the API while offline.

notes: Pasted the brief into the model once, took the first complete answer (localStorage draft + restore banner + beforeunload + backoff retry), dropped it straight into the file, and bolted a one-line offline-tolerance check onto the same prompt when the update came in without re-architecting anything.
